facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s presented with a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption that had lasted 1 month
scaly, crusted pink plaques that involved the periorbital skin
Punch biopsy from the left upper eyelid demonstrated vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL)

scaly, crusted pink plaques that involved the periorbital skin

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques, along with a history of lupus nephritis and biopsy results showing vacuolar interface dermatitis, is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

The patient's history of acute myeloid leukemia and presentation of scaly, crusted pink plaques, along with biopsy results showing epidermal atrophy, could be consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
The patient's history of lupus nephritis and treatment with hydroxychloroquine and lenalidomide, which can induce lupus-like symptoms, is consistent with drug-induced lupus erythematosus.

The patient's history of acute myeloid leukemia and presentation of scaly, crusted pink plaques, along with biopsy results showing vacuolar interface dermatitis, could be consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.
It explains the uncovered finding of deep vein thrombosis.
It explains the uncovered findings of immune thrombocytopenia and diverticulitis, which can be associated with this condition.
